explanation: Vincenzo Peruggia, who had helped fit the museum's glass cases, hid it for over two years. The poet Guillaume Apollinaire was briefly jailed as a suspect, and Picasso was questioned.

claims.text: The Mona Lisa was stolen from the Louvre in August 1911 by Vincenzo Peruggia, who had worked at the museum.
The Mona Lisa was not stolen by a famous painter, a Swiss art dealer or a French art critic.
Peruggia had helped install glass cases for paintings at the Louvre.
The Mona Lisa was missing for more than two years, until it was recovered in Florence in December 1913.
Guillaume Apollinaire was briefly jailed as a suspect in the theft, and Picasso was questioned by police.
